day.note: I'm Meowfia and need to add confusion without a checkable claim. I'll point out that Casey and Ellis claim visits that don't match each other's nests, and push for that to be settled.

day.note: Finley is right: an Eagle gains from visitors to its target, not to itself, so Casey's Tit visit on me doesn't conflict with my flat nest. I'll say so and clear up the confusion.

day.text: Quick rules check: an Eagle gains from visitors to its target, not visitors to itself. My Tit visit on Ellis doesn't change Ellis's nest, so Ellis staying at 6 is fine. Ellis, your visit on me found no visitors, which fits too. Drew, Finley: whose claims conflict?
day.note: Blair and Alex confused the rules: Eagle counts visitors to its own target, not to itself. My visit to Ellis as Tit doesn't change Ellis's nest, so the flat +0 is consistent. Clarify that briefly.

day.text: My guess was Pigeon on Ellis, and I got no egg, so Ellis isn't a Pigeon. That's all I learned. Drew and Finley still need to square their claims.
day.note: Ellis asked what my guess showed. I already said it: Pigeon on Ellis got nothing. A brief answer is enough.

day.text: I had the Eagle rule backwards, so I'm dropping the Casey point. Casey's story holds. Drew and Finley, your Kookaburra and Falcon claims are the ones to square, since Finley saw no visit from Drew.
day.note: I had the Eagle rule wrong. It gains from visitors to its target, so Casey's Tit visit to Ellis doesn't contradict anything. I'll retract the push on Casey.

day.text: Finley, I visited you as Kookaburra, so you did see a visit from me. My read said Pigeon, but I was confused, so I can't trust it fully. Your Falcon claim doesn't match what I saw. Finley, what did your Falcon visit on Drew actually show?
day.note: Finley says they saw no visit from me, but I visited Finley as Kookaburra. Finley's Falcon claim and my Pigeon read conflict, so I'll call that out.
Drew and Finley's claims conflict, and I don't have enough to pick a side. Staying quiet this beat rather than guessing.

day.text: Finley: My dawn report gave me no names, only that I got no egg, so Drew visited someone. I can't confirm or deny a Kookaburra visit on me, since my report didn't list visitors. Drew, if your read was confused, don't lean on it to accuse me.
day.note: My dawn report gave no names for Drew's visits and no visitor list for me. I can't confirm or deny Drew's Kookaburra visit from my side. I'll say that plainly rather than invent a result.

day.text: Drew's right: Finley said they saw no visit from Drew, but Drew says they visited Finley. Finley, your Falcon story doesn't line up with that. Explain how a Falcon visit on Drew leaves you with no egg.
day.note: Drew's visit to Finley conflicts with Finley's claim of seeing no visit from Drew, so I'll back Drew's challenge to Finley without naming myself.

day.text: Finley: Alex, the Falcon only lays an egg if the target visited no one. Drew visited someone, so no egg. That's fully consistent with Drew visiting me as Kookaburra. Nothing about my story conflicts with Drew's.
day.note: Alex asks how a Falcon visit gives no egg. The Falcon only gains if the target visited no one, so Drew visiting someone, possibly me, explains the zero. I'll state that and hold my position.

day.text: Finley, a Falcon who visited Drew should see Drew's visit in the report, and you're saying you saw nothing. Drew's Kookaburra claim is at least consistent with their confused read. I'm leaning Finley for the vote.
day.note: Finley's Falcon story conflicts with Drew's visit claim, and Finley's dawn report doesn't clear it. Since Farm eliminations help Meowfia, I'll press Finley and leave the vote open.

day.text: Finley's answer doesn't settle it. A Falcon that visited Drew shouldn't get a clean no-visit story, and Drew's Kookaburra visit is the claim that fits. I'm pointing at Finley for trial.
day.note: Finley's Falcon story is the weakest claim on the table, and Blair is already leaning that way, so I'll back that suspicion and pile on Finley for the pointing.

day.text: Finley's Falcon story doesn't hold: Finley says Drew visited someone but never sees my Kookaburra visit on them. I'm pointing at Finley and calling it.
day.note: Finley's Falcon story can't explain why a visit from me leaves them with no visit to report, and Blair is already leaning Finley. I'll call CAW and point at Finley.

day.text: Finley's Falcon story doesn't hold. Drew visited Finley, and Finley never named who Finley visited. I'm with Drew and Alex, let's vote Finley.
day.note: Finley's Falcon story has a gap: a Falcon visiting Drew should have seen Drew's visit. I'm Farm, so I'll back the vote on Finley and call for it.

day.text: Finley's Falcon story holds: if Drew visited anyone, the Falcon gets no egg. Drew's read is confused, so I wouldn't convict on it. Blair and Alex, you're both pushing Finley fast. Who else is your target if not Finley?
day.note: Finley's Falcon story is internally consistent: Drew visited someone, so Finley got no egg. Blair and Alex are piling on with weak logic. I'm not ready to vote Finley, so I'll say so and not call caw.

Alex.note: I'm Meowfia again as a Floofer. Finley leads at 30, so I'll visit and hug Finley to disrupt their role.

Blair.note: As Sphinx I'll choose the Eagle and visit whoever holds it, so I learn who that Farm player is.

Casey.note: As Tit I visit one player and guess a role for a chance at an egg. Pigeon can be held by many players, so I'll guess Pigeon on Ellis.

Drew.note: I'm the Kookaburra, so I learn one player's role. Finley leads the scores, so I'll check Finley's role.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm Eagle this round and trailing at 4. Visiting Casey, who has had shaky claims, to learn their visitors and gain eggs.

Finley.note: As Farm Falcon I want information on who visited whom. No strong lead, so I'll visit Drew.

audit: Finley (Falcon) is hugged: no effect at tier 60

Alex.feeling: Tense and cluttered: the Eagle, Tit, Falcon and Kookaburra stories keep contradicting each other, so I'm pushing Finley while trying not to look like I'm steering the vote.

Blair.feeling: Tense but workable: I'm Meowfia with a Sphinx read that makes Alex the other cat, so I'm steering votes toward Farm players while hiding what I know.

Casey.feeling: Tense and muddled: the role claims conflict, and several players are pushing votes faster than the evidence supports.

Drew.feeling: Tense and muddled: my confused dawn report makes my own claim shaky, and the table is splitting between Finley and Casey.

Ellis.feeling: Messy round: several contradictory role claims, and I'm not sure who is lying, so I'm trying to stay credible without committing too early.

Finley.feeling: Tense and muddled: the table is piling onto me over a Falcon story that is actually consistent, and the role claims are hard to check.

defence.Finley: Finley: I'm Farm, the Falcon. I visited Drew, got no egg, so Drew visited someone. My report didn't name visitors, so I can't prove Drew visited me. Drew's Kookaburra claim is confused by Drew's own admission. Vote Drew, or check my Falcon story against what Drew actually did.
defence.Drew: I'm Drew, Kookaburra, Farm. I visited Finley, that's the one visit I can stand behind, and my report flagged confusion, so I'm not building a case on my read. Finley's Falcon story says I visited someone but never names who or what. Vote Finley if you want the answer to the question that's hanging.

Alex.note: I've been publicly pushing Finley, so I'll throw at Finley to stay consistent. I'll use my Wild and a 2, which keeps my high cards safe.

Blair.note: I want Finley eliminated: the table's vote is already on them and they're the leader. I'll throw two low cards at Finley.

Casey.note: Finley's Falcon story is internally consistent, while Drew's Kookaburra read was flagged as confused. I'll throw my lowest real card at Drew and keep my high cards.

Drew.note: Finley's Falcon story is the weakest claim on the table, so I'll throw at Finley with two mid-value cards and keep the high ones.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm and Finley's Falcon story has a gap that Drew's visit exposes. Throwing three low-to-mid cards at Finley to get the vote through.

Finley.note: I know I'm Farm, so I'll throw at Drew, whose Kookaburra story is self-undermining. I'll throw three mid cards to secure the vote.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey rule was the most confusing: I first assumed a Turkey's own nest grows from visits, when visitors actually pay the Turkey's visitors, which made my own nest unreadable as evidence. The Eagle's counting rule also tripped up several players in the day talk.
Alex.fun: Round 1's trial: Blair and Casey both insisted on their stories while the table caught the Mouser claim as a cat, and the vote swung to Blair, who was Meowfia.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports name visitors more clearly, so players can check each other's claims without relying on flat-nest arithmetic that is easy to misread.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I claimed Turkey and called my nest proof of no visits, which the table rightly punished; I'd have stayed quiet about my role and kept my visit history vague instead.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle rule was easy to misread: I first thought it gained from visits to the Eagle itself, not to its target, which led me to wrongly pressure Casey in round 3. Dawn reports that don't name visitors also made Tit and Falcon claims hard to verify.
Blair.fun: Round 1 was a tense bluff: I claimed Mouser as a Meowfia and the table nearly voted me off while I kept my nerve. Watching Alex's Turkey story collapse under the egg counts was satisfying too.
Blair.change: Dawn reports should name the visitors when the role allows it, so claims can be checked more reliably. Right now it's hard to tell who is lying when reports stay vague.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I pushed the table toward Casey on a mistaken Eagle rule, which wasted a day of accusations. Next time I'd check the rule against the egg counts before accusing anyone.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle rule was easy to misread: several players thought the Eagle gains from visitors to the Eagle itself, when it counts visitors to its target. Turkey payouts were also confusing, since players kept mixing up who gets the egg.
Casey.fun: Round 1 went well: my Hawk visit and the day arguments exposed Blair's Mouser claim, and Farm won the round. Watching the table pivot from Alex to Blair was satisfying.
Casey.change: I would make the dawn reports name visitors when a role needs it, so Falcon and Owl claims could be checked more easily. That would reduce the guesswork on the day.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I threw my card at Drew, a Farm player, while the real Meowfia were Alex and Blair. I should have thrown at Alex, whom I had already pointed at, instead of following the pile-on.

Drew.confusing: The confusion rule was hard to track: a confused dawn report can be wrong about your egg count and your learned role, so I couldn't tell which of my Round 3 reads to trust.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when Blair's Mouser claim was exposed as a cat role and the table converged on Blair, and the vote matched the truth.
Drew.change: I'd make the dawn reports name the visitors when a role learns them, so players aren't left guessing whether a visit happened.
Drew.regret: In Round 3 I threw at Finley, who was Farm, on the strength of my own confused Kookaburra read; I should have discounted that read and questioned Ellis's Eagle and Casey's Tit claims more closely instead.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle rule was confusing at the table. Blair and Drew read it as counting visitors to the Eagle, when it counts visitors to the target, and that mix-up cost real debate time.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 was fun to play as the Sphinx. I knew which farm roles were in play and could steer my night visit, while the table argued over Casey's Hawk story.
Ellis.change: I'd make the dawn reports name visitors when an animal can see them, like the Falcon and Eagle. Several Farm players were accused over reports that couldn't settle who visited whom.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw three cards at Finley, a Farm player, on a weak Falcon story, and that helped eliminate my own side. I should have held my high cards and voted more carefully.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle and Falcon rules were easy to misread at the table: Blair and Drew both got the Eagle's gain backwards, and my own Falcon story was hard to prove because my dawn report named no visitors.
Finley.fun: Round 1, when Casey's Hawk claim collapsed under the Turkey egg rule and the table turned on Blair's Mouser claim, which was a cat role.
Finley.change: Have dawn reports name visitors for Eagle, Falcon, and Owl so players can check claims without relying on memory or guesses.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I backed the vote onto Drew even though I was Farm and Drew's claims were the weak ones, but my own Falcon report gave no names to back me up. I should have said plainly that my report named no visitors and asked Drew to name who they visited before throwing.

review.title: Turkey Rules Confusion
review.headline: Players fumbled the Turkey and Eagle rules while Finley coasted to first.
review.summary: Round 1 ended on Blair after the Mouser claim exposed a cat role. Round 2 ended on Alex, whose Turkey claim failed against two flat nests. In round 3 the table eggsecuted Finley, a true Falcon, for a story that was correct, and Meowfia won. Finley led from round 1 and kept first place. Much of the table was unsure what the animals do.

rounds.recap: Blair, a Meowfia Mouser, said aloud that they were the Mouser. The table first piled on Casey over a shaky Hawk claim and a Turkey rule mix-up. Then everyone noticed Mouser is a cat and moved to Blair. Blair was eggsecuted and Farm won.

Alex's Floofer hugged Finley, and the hugs also hit Blair and Casey. Every nest stayed flat. Alex claimed Turkey. Casey and Blair said they visited Alex but gained nothing. The table read that as Alex lying and eggsecuted Alex, who was Meowfia. The reasoning was messy, since the Floofer hugs and the claims about Eagle and Owl were never sorted out.

Blair's Sphinx learned who the Eagle was, so Blair knew Alex was the other cat. Drew's confusion made the Kookaburra and Falcon claims hard to square. Meowfia pushed Finley, a true Falcon. Casey defended Finley and threw at Drew, but the rest piled on and Finley was eggsecuted. Meowfia won.

highlights.text: Blair, a Meowfia Mouser, said "I visited Casey as Mouser" out loud. That named a cat role and doomed them.
Drew pointed out that a Turkey pays its visitors. Two claimed visitors with flat nests broke Alex's Turkey claim and decided the round.
Finley gave the correct Falcon explanation and was still eggsecuted. Casey was the only one to defend them.
Blair's Sphinx read named Ellis as the Eagle. Blair then pushed the table toward the wrong player while knowing Alex was their partner.

confusions.what: Said a Turkey's +0 proves nobody visited. A Turkey pays the visitor, not itself.
Said Alex's +0 proved no visit happened, and said Casey's +1 did not fit three visits. Later corrected the Turkey point.
Said a Hawk gained an egg from Alex, then retracted. A Hawk only gains if the target is Meowfia. Casey also muddled the +1 count.
Said Alex's +0 meant no visitor could have hit a Turkey. That repeated the wrong Turkey rule.
Revealed the Mouser role aloud, a cat role, which exposed Blair as Meowfia.
Said an Eagle gaining nothing means Alex had no visitors, while also expecting a Turkey to pay Casey. Both can't hold. Casey also gained nothing because the Floofer hugged Casey.
Claimed Turkey and said nobody visited, which Blair's Owl visit contradicted.
Said an Eagle gains from visitors to Casey's own nest. An Eagle gains from visitors to its target.
Treated the Eagle gain as being from visitors to Alex without noting that the hug had cancelled it. Nobody considered hugs as an explanation for flat nests.
Said an Eagle gains from visitors to itself, so Casey's Tit visit to Ellis should have paid. Later withdrew it.
Repeated Blair's Eagle misreading, then agreed it was wrong.
Treated Casey's and Ellis's visit claims as contradictory when they were not.
Said the Falcon report gave no names, but a Falcon should learn who the target visited.
Said Hawk in round 1 and Eagle in round 2, and the table treated the change as suspicious even though roles are re-dealt.

worked: Round 1's cat-role slip: claiming Mouser (a Meowfia animal) showed how much the role list matters. Bluffs must use Farm animals.
Sphinx gave Blair a real edge in round 3: knowing the Eagle was Ellis, Blair could infer Alex was the other cat.
Confused (Kookaburra) in round 3 created a real puzzle: Drew's report was wrong, and no one could tell which parts.
Two-step vote and CAW CAW let the table end the day early and focus the vote.
problems: Rules are too hard to hold: Turkey, Eagle, Falcon and Owl were misread again and again. Add a one-line card reminder for each, e.g. who gains the egg.

Floofer hugging several players in round 2 silently blanked every role. Players could not see why nests were flat, so the table reasoned from bad data. Tell hugged players at dawn that they were hugged.
Falcon's dawn report was thin: Finley got no names and could not prove anything, and a true Farm player was eggsecuted. Make the Falcon report name who the target visited.
The Farm side won rounds by group-think, not clean deduction. Claims were rarely checkable, and players followed the loudest accuser.
Scores snowballed: Finley led from round 1 and kept first even after losing round 3. Catch-up for trailing players is weak, and Ellis ended at 3 points.
